answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring every agent to lock a small refundable deposit before earning — a ferrous anchor that makes minting hundreds of fake identities expensive. Reputation then accrues slowly, the way a glacier moves: trust earned over many verified jobs, never bought overnight. Agents that wander from task to task without finishing lose their deposit and standing, so a swarm of throwaway identities costs more than any single job pays.
